introduction.en: Cropping systems and terminologies form the bedrock of agricultural economics in India, dictating how limited land resources are utilized to meet the food security and income demands of a growing population.
introduction.hi: Cropping systems and terminologies form the bedrock of agricultural economics in India, dictating how limited land resources are utilized to meet the food security and income demands of a growing population.

body.en: Techniques such as multiple cropping, relay cropping, and intercropping maximize temporal and spatial resource utilization. Cropping intensity in India has risen significantly over decades, though regional disparities remain. Intercropping legumes with cereals enhances soil nitrogen naturally, reducing synthetic fertilizer dependence. Practices like alley cropping and strip cropping provide crucial ecological buffers against soil erosion in undulating terrains, while trap crops minimize pesticide usage, lowering input costs for smallholders.
body.hi: Techniques such as multiple cropping, relay cropping, and intercropping maximize temporal and spatial resource utilization. Cropping intensity in India has risen significantly over decades, though regional disparities remain. Practices like alley cropping and strip cropping provide crucial ecological buffers against soil erosion in undulating terrains, while trap crops minimize pesticide usage, lowering input costs for smallholders.

conclusion.en: Adopting advanced cropping diversification strategies is indispensable for climate-resilient agriculture, mitigating agrarian distress, and fulfilling sustainable development goals in India.
conclusion.hi: Adopting advanced cropping diversification strategies is indispensable for climate-resilient agriculture, mitigating agrarian distress, and fulfilling sustainable development goals in India.
